Generation of a neutral partition given parameter \(\theta\) using the Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey representation

Source: R/generation.R
generate_hoppe_urn.Rd

generate_hoppe_urn() creates a rank-abundance distribution for a given \(\theta\) and J. Beta-distributed random variables are drawn from \(Beta(1,\theta)\) to build the stick-breaking weights of the Griffiths-Engen-McCloskey (GEM) distribution, and the partition is a multinomial draw of J individuals according to these weights. Its cost does not depend on J (up to the multinomial draw), which makes it suitable for very large samples (10^12 individuals and beyond).

The draw is exact: sticks are generated in blocks until every individual has been assigned. The total number of individuals is always exactly J.

Usage

generate_hoppe_urn(theta, J)

Arguments

theta

parameter \(\theta\), a positive real value

J

number of individuals, a whole number (up to 2^53)

Value

A list with

abundance

the species abundances, sorted in decreasing order and summing to J

k

the expected number of species for these parameters (see kest()); the number of species in this particular draw is length(abundance)

Examples

set.seed(1)
out <- generate_hoppe_urn(11.3, 234373)
length(out$abundance) # close to out$k
#> [1] 123
